NAVAREA / NAVTEX STATIONS

Voyage

  1. Choose the departure and arrival ports.
  2. Set the speed and the ETD in local time (LT) – the zone times fill in from the ports.
  3. Tap Plan route – results appear below the button.
Ocean crossings use great circle sailing automatically – change it on the chart with ✎. Plan, Waypoints, ETA and Weather are in the bottom bar; the other tools are in the ☰ menu. Tap a section title to fold it.
Zone time (ZT) is the correction from local time to UTC: UTC = LT + ZT.
  • East longitude → minus (Manila UTC+8 → ZT −8)
  • West longitude → plus (Seattle UTC−8 → ZT +8; in summer time UTC−7 → +7)
Filled in automatically from the port's time zone, including daylight saving time on the departure / arrival date. Type another value if the ship keeps a different time; clear the box to go back to the automatic value.
Everything you enter is saved automatically on this phone.

Great circle settings

Plan a route to choose where the great circle starts and ends.

Route optimisation (ECA)
–

Each nm inside a 0.10% S zone is weighted by its extra cost, so the route stays outside the ECA while that is cheaper and crosses the limit at the best point. Zones: North American, US Caribbean, North Sea, Baltic, Mediterranean (Norwegian Sea from 1 Mar 2027). A scrubber ticked on the Voyage Draft page removes the penalty.

Waypoints

Plan a route on the Passage Plan page first.

How to use
  1. Enter the departure drafts, densities, consumption and tank quantities.
  2. Distances, speed, ECA legs and zone times fill in from the passage plan. The daily drafts and ROB appear at the bottom.

Departure

Zone time (ZT): East −, West +. e.g. UTC+8 = −8, UTC−5 = +5. The ETA uses the difference between the two zones. LPP comes from the imported vessel data.

Route & speed

Route
Diesel on the two ECA legs; 0 = the port is outside any ECA. Speed from the passage plan is the average over the whole passage (slower berth ↔ pilot and in canals), so the ETA here matches the plan.

Local port fuel rules

Some ports require distillate (diesel / MGO) inside port limits, e.g. Singapore and Kaohsiung. The diesel leg is added to the ECA legs (diesel replaces FO). Blank = no local rule.
How the local port fuel rules work
  1. Ports with a known rule fill in automatically (Singapore; Taiwan ports such as Kaohsiung, Keelung, Taichung).
  2. For any other port, enter the distance from the berth (nm) inside which the port requires distillate (DO / MGO). Leave it blank if there is no rule.
  3. That distance, counted from the berth, is burned as diesel even outside an ECA. It is shown as a DIESEL leg in the fuel legs and in the daily ROB.
  4. Plan the changeover so it is complete before that point; record the time, position and ROB in the logbook.
  5. Rules change – confirm with the agent / latest port circular before arrival.

Ballast operations (optional)

Qty: + ballast in, − ballast out. Date & time is in departure zone time. Mid G fills in automatically from the Quick Draft tank of the same name and stays in sync with it.
Tank quantities are what is on board at departure. Consumption is taken from the first tank until empty, then the next. Mid G: − forward, + aft of midship.
How to calculate the ETA
  1. Choose what to calculate: Berth to berth, Berth to arrival pilot station or Pilot to pilot. With a planned or imported route the distance, speed, departure time and zone times fill in (↻ refills).
  2. Enter the departure date & time (LT), the zone times, the distance to go and the speed.
  3. Enter a required ETA to get the speed needed and the margin. Tap any result to see the working.
Steaming time= Distance ÷ Speed
ETA (UTC)= Departure (LT) + ZT departure + Steaming time
ETA (LT)= ETA (UTC) − ZT arrival
Speed required= Distance ÷ Time available
Margin= Required ETA − ETA

How to use Sunrise / Sunset
  1. Tap ☀ in the bottom bar: it opens today at your GPS position. The bar shows today's sunrise–sunset.
  2. For another place or day pick a waypoint of the route or type the position and date.
  3. Check the zone time (set from the longitude); change it if the ship keeps a different time.
Sunrise / sunset= sun's upper limb on the horizon (−0.83°)
Civil twilight= sun 6° below the horizon
Nautical twilight= sun 12° below
Astronomical twilight= sun 18° below
LT= UTC − ZD

Position & date

Opens with today's date at your GPS position. You can also pick a waypoint (its position, zone time and the local date at its ETA) or type any position: degrees, minutes and tap N/S – E/W. Zone time: East −, West +. All times are local time (LT).

How to use the sailing calculators
  1. Choose a calculator in the tab bar.
  2. Type each position in its boxes: degrees, minutes, then tap the letter to switch N/S or E/W. Courses in °T, speeds in knots.
  3. Results update as you type. ↻ From route takes the pilot-to-pilot positions of the planned route.
Great circle: cos D = sinφ₁ sinφ₂ + cosφ₁ cosφ₂ cos dλ; initial course tan C = sin dλ / (cosφ₁ tanφ₂ − sinφ₁ cos dλ); vertex cos φv = cosφ₁ sin C.
Mercator: tan C = d.long′ / DMP; distance = d.lat′ / cos C; MP = 7915.7045 log tan(45° + φ/2) − 23.2689 sin φ − 0.0525 sin³φ (WGS 84).
Parallel: departure = d.long′ × cos φ.
DR / EP: DR = course and speed through the water from the last fix; EP = DR + leeway + current (set and drift) → course and speed made good.
Composite: GC to the limiting latitude (cos dλ = tan φ / tan φL, cos D = sin φ / sin φL), parallel sailing along it, GC to the destination.

Great circle sailing

Illustration
A = departure, B = destination. The great circle bends towards the pole and is shorter; the course changes all the time, so waypoints are set along it. C = initial course, V = vertex.

Mercator sailing

Illustration
The rhumb line is a straight line on the Mercator chart. The big triangle (DMP, d.long) gives the course C; the small one (d.lat, departure) gives the distance.

Parallel sailing

Illustration
Sailing east or west along one parallel. The meridians close in towards the pole, so the distance (departure) is d.long × cos latitude.

Dead reckoning (DR)

Illustration
DR = position from the last fix using only the course steered and the speed through the water for the time run. No current, wind or leeway.

Estimated position (EP)

Illustration
EP = DR corrected for leeway (wind) and the current: set = direction the current flows to, drift = its speed. The line Fix → EP is the course and speed made good.

Composite sailing

Illustration
Used when the great circle goes beyond a safe latitude (ice, weather). GC from A to the limit (V1), parallel sailing along it to V2, then GC to B.
How to use the weather
  1. Along the route: plan a route – the forecast for the ship's ETA at each point downloads automatically (wind 16 days, sea 8 days). Tap WX on the chart to show it on the map.
  2. At a position: tap GPS or type a position to get the next 3 days.
Open-Meteo (DWD, ECMWF, NOAA models), CC BY 4.0. Planning aid – use official forecasts (SafetyNET / NAVTEX / weather routing) for navigation.

How to calculate the safety depth
  1. Enter the maximum static draft (↻ takes the deepest draft from the Voyage Draft Plan) and the squat (↻ takes it from the Squat page).
  2. Enter the heave / swell allowance and any other allowance (heel, FW, waves).
  3. Enter the required UKC from the company SMS / port rules, in metres or as % of draft.
  4. Set the ECDIS safety depth and safety contour to the values shown; shallow ≈ draft, deep ≈ 2 × draft.
Required UKC= Draft × % ÷ 100 (or the metres entered)
Safety depth= Draft + Squat + UKC + Heave + Other
Safety contour= next ENC contour ≥ Safety depth
Shallow contour= Draft (rounded up)
Deep contour= 2 × Draft (rounded up)

Ship

Required UKC per company SMS / port rules (e.g. 10 % of draft at sea, 0.5–1.0 m in port, more in open roads with swell).

How to calculate the squat
  1. Enter LPP, breadth, static draft, block coefficient Cb and the speed through the water.
  2. Choose open water or confined / canal; enter the water depth (and the channel width for a canal).
  3. Read the squat and the dynamic draft; the table gives the squat at other speeds. Tap “Use in Safety depth” to carry it over.
Blockage factor S= (B × T) ÷ (W × h)
W (open water)= (7.7 + 20 × (1 − Cb)²) × B
Squat δ= Cb × S^0.81 × V^2.08 ÷ 20
Dynamic draft= Draft + Squat

Ship

Cb typical: bulk carrier / tanker 0.80–0.85, general cargo 0.70, container 0.60–0.65. Speed is through the water (not over ground).

Water

Channel
Open water: the width of influence FB = (7.7 + 20(1 − Cb)²) × B is used as W. Confined: enter the channel width at the bottom (canal / dredged channel).

NAVAREA warnings (live)

About the live warnings
Downloaded automatically when the app opens and every 3 hours, and revalidated weekly: if the list has not been rechecked for 7 days its warnings are hidden. Cancelled messages ("CANCEL THIS MSG …", "CANCEL HYDROPAC …") are removed automatically, and warnings older than the age filter on the map panel are hidden. NAVTEX and local warnings you add must be confirmed as still in force once a week. Active warnings from the US NGA broadcast service: NAVAREA IV and XII, HYDROPAC (Pacific and Indian Ocean), HYDROLANT and HYDROARC. Positions in the text are plotted on the chart.
Source status
If the download keeps failing

The app first asks NGA directly. If NGA refuses (it often blocks pages opened from a phone), it retries through public relay servers (corsproxy.io, allorigins.win, codetabs.com). On a ship network that blocks these, use one of the two options below.

Manual load: open the NGA feed in the phone browser, save the page (or select all → copy), then load the file or paste it here.

Add NAVTEX / NAVAREA / local warning

Reads positions like 12-34.5N 123-45.6E, 12°34.5'N 123°45.6'E or 1234.5N 12345.6E. "Area bounded by" becomes an area, "between / along / cable" a line, "within X nm of" a circle. Your warnings are kept on this phone only.
